selection_reason: strict mode option -> option character validation -> restricts allowed characters in SRI options
source_summary: Options come from user-provided SRI (Subresource Integrity) strings parsed by regex patterns. In strict mode, options are extracted from match[3] of STRICT_SRI_REGEX which captures characters in the range \x21-\x7E (printable ASCII).
sink_summary: Validated options are joined with '?' and appended to the algorithm-digest string in the toString() output, which may be used in HTML script/link tags for integrity verification.
guard_summary: The validation ensures options contain only visible ASCII characters (\x21-\x7E) when strict mode is enabled. This prevents injection of control characters, whitespace, or non-ASCII characters that could bypass SRI validation or cause parsing issues.
risk_pattern: Strict mode validation enforces RFC-compliant option syntax by restricting options to printable ASCII characters only, preventing potential injection or parsing bypass vulnerabilities in SRI implementations.
used_variable_sources: this.options from constructor parsing of user-provided SRI strings
enclosing_conditions: opts && opts.strict condition enables the validation block
Validation is part of a compound condition with algorithm and digest validation
context_summary: The validation occurs in strict mode toString() method, ensuring SRI options comply with W3C specification for visual characters only, preventing malformed options that could bypass integrity checks.
unresolved_facts: Specific attack scenarios where non-VCHAR options could bypass SRI validation are not detailed in the code comments
